subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to cleanup with `deleteAfterRun: true`, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source bug and UI defaults support cleanup for recurring isolated sessions, but the open strict-validation PR proposes the opposite public contract; automation should not choose that product boundary.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-upgrade/load or doctor coverage so existing omitted jobs are repaired too.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after it reconciles UI, Gateway errors, and legacy recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new-create default and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-upgrade/load or doctor coverage so existing omitted jobs are repaired too.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the most recent current-main history on the cron normalization and persistence surfaces that define this product contract.
